strategy_title: Expand Triton Grid to Cover All SMs
strategy_description: When a Triton kernel launches far fewer blocks than available SMs (e.g., 8 blocks on a 132-SM GPU), most SMs sit idle and achieved occupancy collapses to single digits. Switching from a 1D grid to a 2D grid by tiling the larger problem dimension (e.g., YBLOCK increase + grid Y-axis) distributes work across more SMs and reduces elapsed cycles. The NCU LaunchConfiguration rule with high estimated speedup (>90%) and near-zero achieved occupancy (<10%) are the key signals.
slow_pseudocode:
# 1D grid, only 8 blocks for 132-SM GPU
XBLOCK = 128
YBLOCK = 8
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK),)  # = (8,)
kernel[grid](data, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK=YBLOCK, XBLOCK=XBLOCK)
fast_pseudocode:
# 2D grid, 4096 blocks across 132 SMs (~31 waves)
XBLOCK = 64   # match xnumel exactly
YBLOCK = 2048 # tile large Y dimension
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK), cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK))  # = (1, 4096)
kernel[grid](data, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK=YBLOCK, XBLOCK=XBLOCK)
applicable_when: NCU LaunchConfiguration rule fires with >80% estimated speedup; grid_size << sm_count (e.g., 8 blocks on 132 SMs); achieved_occupancy < 10%; waves_per_sm ~0; kernel has a large secondary dimension (ynumel >> xnumel) that is currently serialized within each block
do_not_apply_when: Grid already covers most SMs (waves_per_sm >= 1); problem size is genuinely tiny and latency is dominated by kernel launch overhead; kernel body does not correctly handle 2D program_id indexing
framework_notes: Triton kernels use tl.program_id(0/1/2) for grid dimensions. If the kernel body already uses program_id(1) and program_id(2) for Y-indexing, switching from a 1D to 2D grid at the launch site requires no kernel body changes. Only the grid tuple and XBLOCK/YBLOCK arguments at the call site need updating. Note: in this case the actual grid_size remained 8 in profiling after (suggesting the plan was only partially applied or the diff was incomplete), yet a modest 5.7% speedup was still observed from minor warp cycle improvements.
